home.introHeadline: "I grew up under Oklahoma skies and grew into myself under New York Lights."
home.introBody: Hi y'all! My name is Hannah Jew. A multi-hyphenate artist based in New York City and telling stories that don't fit in one box. It all started back in my hometown of Oklahoma, separation anxiety almost got the best of me and I'm not quite sure why it was that random day, but after several attempts to stay in the studio without crying, I did and have not looked back ever since. I think it was meant to be that I was going to be a dancer/artist. I love everything about the arts: the process, what happens behind the scenes and the magic onstage. I'm always excited to meet new people and experience new things. As I continue to evolve as a person and artist, I'm so excited to see all the unexpected and beautiful experiences that are yet to come. Maybe you'll be a stepping stone in my journey too! about.lead: Hannah Jew (周健倫) is a New York City based multi-hyphenate artist, educator and frequent collaborator with other creative disciplines.
paragraphs: Trained at The University of Oklahoma (BFA, Ballet Performance) and shaped by intensives with Complexions Contemporary Ballet, the Joffrey Ballet, American Ballet Theatre, San Francisco Ballet and Tulsa Ballet, Hannah has danced professionally with Nai-Ni Chen Dance Company, Ballet Hispánico (BHdos), Dayton Ballet, and Oklahoma City Ballet.

Her choreographic and stage-direction work centers stories from the Asian-American experience, with projects at the Museum of Chinese in America, China Institute, National Asian Artists Project, and New York Theatre Workshop. As an educator, she teaches dance to all ages and experience levels, including individuals with disabilities.

On stage, she has toured nationally with The King and I (dir. Bartlett Sher, chor. Christopher Gattelli), performed with the New York City Opera, danced at New York Fashion Week, and appeared in a world premiere at the Smithsonian's National Museum of Asian Art, as both dancer and choreographer.
She is a proud member of Actors' Equity Association and is represented by Clear Talent Group.
